ex-cm04-harmonic-motion-check.title: "A harmonic model on explicit data: the sinusoid, its least period, the conserved energy and the phase ellipse checked at $m=1$, $k=4$"
ex-cm04-harmonic-motion-check.physical_scope: "A worked check of the harmonic model at the declared data m=1 kg, k=4 N/m, datum (0, 0 m, 1 m/s): the displayed sinusoid is the unique maximal motion, its amplitude and phase, least period, frequency, conserved energy and phase ellipse are computed from the general theorem, and the energy identity is verified directly. The item asserts no measured value and no claim that a real oscillator realizes the model."

ex-cm04-pendulum-small-angle-check.title: "The ideal pendulum as an effective one-dimensional model: strict minimum, stability, the small-angle harmonic model and the finite-time error bound with its numbers"
ex-cm04-pendulum-small-angle-check.physical_scope: "A worked check of the effective one-dimensional pendulum model m l^2 theta-ddot = -m g l sin(theta) adopted from the recorded source: the potential presentation with U=-m g l cos(theta), the equilibria, the strict minimum at theta=0 and the Lyapunov stability of the hanging rest point, the linearised harmonic model with frequency sqrt(g/l), the finite-time small-angle error bound with explicit constants at g=l=1, and the failure of conservation of the harmonic energy along the exact motion. The item asserts no measured value, no period formula for finite amplitudes and no derivation of the effective equation from the constrained system."

ex-cm04-resonance-response-check.title: "A driven oscillator on explicit data: the steady response, its amplitude maximum and a worked transient at $m=k=1$, $f_0=1$, $c=0.2$, $\\Omega=1$"
ex-cm04-resonance-response-check.physical_scope: "A worked check of the driven oscillator at the declared data m=k=1, f_0=1 N, c=0.2 kg/s, Omega=1 rad/s: the steady response 5 sin t and its verification by substitution, the amplitude 5 m at the drive frequency against the maximum value of the amplitude function and its location, the phase lag, the transient motion from rest and its exponential approach to the steady response, and the comparison with the undamped cases. The item asserts no measured value and no claim about a physical apparatus."

ex-cm05-barycentric-orbits-check.title: "Barycentric orbits of two unequal masses on declared model data: $p_1=(m_2/M)p$, $p_2=(m_1/M)p$, semiaxes in the ratio $3:1$ and areal rates in the ratio $9:1$"
ex-cm05-barycentric-orbits-check.physical_scope: "A numerical check of the barycentric reconstruction on declared model data with unequal masses: the two labels' conic parameters and semimajor axes, the common eccentricity and focus at the centre of mass, the ratio of the areal rates $(m_2/m_1)^2$ and the common period about the centre of mass. Every number is declared model data or an exact consequence of the cited items; no observation or measurement is used."

ex-cm05-circular-orbit-frequency-check.title: "A gravitational circular relative orbit checked on declared model data: $r_0=2\\cdot10^{6}\\,$m, $\\mu r_0\\omega^2=u'(r_0)=3\\cdot10^{12}\\,$N, $E=-3\\cdot10^{18}\\,$J and $\\omega_{\\rm lin}=\\omega=10^{-9}\\,$s$^{-1}$"
ex-cm05-circular-orbit-frequency-check.physical_scope: "A numerical check of the circular-orbit criterion and the linearised radial frequency on declared model data for the gravitational relative problem: the critical radius, the force-balance identity $\\mu r_0\\omega^2=u'(r_0)$, the energy at the minimum of the effective potential, the equality $\\omega_{\\rm lin}=\\omega$ for the inverse-square potential, and the two labels' circular motions about the centre of mass. Every number is declared model data or an exact consequence of the cited items; no observation is used and no nonlinear stability is claimed."

ex-cm05-gravitational-ellipse-and-period.title: "An elliptic gravitational relative orbit checked on declared model data: $p=10^{6}\\,$m, $e=3/5$, $a=25\\cdot10^{6}/16\\,$m, $b=5\\cdot10^{6}/4\\,$m, $E=-3.2\\cdot10^{17}\\,$J and $T=125\\pi\\cdot10^{9}/32\\,$s, with $T^{2}=4\\pi^{2}a^{3}/(G_{\\mathrm N}M)$"
ex-cm05-gravitational-ellipse-and-period.physical_scope: "A numerical consistency check of the elliptic-branch formulas of the adopted gravitational two-label model on declared model data: the conic parameter, semiaxes, energy, period by two routes, the third-law form $T^2=4\\pi^2a^3/(G_{\\mathrm N}M)$ under the declared mass identification, the areal rate and the barycentric semiaxes. Every number is a declared model datum or an exact consequence of the cited items; the example asserts no observation, no measurement and no applicability of the model to any real system."

ex-cm05-parabolic-and-hyperbolic-branch-.title: "The parabolic and hyperbolic branches on declared model data: $E=0$ with $e=1$ and periapsis $p/2$, and $E=1.5\\cdot10^{18}\\,$J with $e=2$, periapsis $p/3$ and angular domain $\\lvert\\theta-\\theta_0\\rvert<2\\pi/3$"
ex-cm05-parabolic-and-hyperbolic-branch-.physical_scope: "A numerical consistency check of the zero- and positive-energy branches of the gravitational relative orbit on declared model data: the eccentricity-energy correspondence $E=0\\iff e=1$ and $E>0\\iff e>1$, the periapsis distances as zeros of the effective potential, the angular domain of the hyperbolic branch and the barrier bound. Every number is declared model data or an exact consequence of the cited items; no observation, no asymptotics and no scattering cross-section is claimed."

ex-cm06-bead-on-a-rotating-wire.title: "A bead on a uniformly rotating straight wire: the rheonomic ideal constraint, its reaction, and the work it performs"
ex-cm06-bead-on-a-rotating-wire.physical_scope: "A worked model check of the rheonomic ideal-constraint branch: one label of mass m constrained without friction to a straight wire through the origin that rotates uniformly in a horizontal plane, under the declared uniform downward field; the verification exhibits the unique maximal constrained motion through consistent data, computes the multiplier and the reaction, verifies the reaction-power identity and the mechanical-energy balance, and shows on explicit model data that an ideal rheonomic constraint performs positive work. The example is a model computation with declared idealizations (frictionless bead, massless rigid wire, prescribed uniform rotation, uniform field with the wire supporting the weight); every number is a model value, not a measurement."

ex-cm06-pendulum-tension-and-reaction-po.title: "The planar pendulum as an ideal holonomic model: the multiplier, the tension and the vanishing reaction power of a scleronomic constraint"
ex-cm06-pendulum-tension-and-reaction-po.physical_scope: "A worked model check of the holonomic ideal-constraint branch: a mass point constrained without friction to a circle of radius l in a vertical plane about a fixed pivot under a declared uniform downward field, realized as a bead on a smooth circular wire, with the explicit two-component multiplier (the component tied to the constraining plane vanishing along the motion), the reaction read as the tension along the link, the standard pendulum equation obtained by projecting the constrained equation, the identically vanishing reaction power of the scleronomic constraint, and the conservation of the mechanical energy on explicit model data. The example is a model computation with the declared idealizations (smooth massless wire, equivalently a rigid link or a taut string while it stays taut; frictionless pivot; uniform field); every number is a model value, not a measurement, and the empirical status of a string that can go slack (or of a link that can buckle) is recorded as a limitation of the model."

ex-cm06-rolling-disk-model-comparison.title: "Rolling as distinct models: the planar ideal no-slip disk against frictionless sliding, and the contact capability condition"
ex-cm06-rolling-disk-model-comparison.physical_scope: "A worked model-discrimination example for the rolling contact: two reduced planar models of a disk with the same declared kinetic matrix and applied force — the ideal no-slip model with its holonomic constraint and ideal reaction, and the frictionless sliding model with no constraint — with the accelerations, the multiplier, the required contact force and the empirical static-friction capability condition compared on explicit model data. The example uses a reduced two-coordinate description declared as model data, asserts no measured value, and records that general three-dimensional rolling, slip transitions and contact changes are separate models outside it."

ex-cm06-rotating-chart-inertial-terms.title: "All four inertial terms checked on explicit data, and the exact return to an inertial chart"
ex-cm06-rotating-chart-inertial-terms.physical_scope: "A worked finite check of the moving-chart equation of the framework: a zero-force one-label model observed in a chart with a uniformly accelerated rotation angle and a uniformly accelerated reference curve; the four inertial terms are evaluated term by term at one time and compared with the inertial-chart acceleration of the motion, a chart with nonzero angular velocity is identified as non-inertial by the criterion, and an explicit chart with affine reference curve and constant rotation is checked to reproduce the inertial-frame description. All values are model values; the example reports no measurement."

ex-cm07-free-particle-straight-lines.title: "The free particle: the unique stationary curve between fixed endpoints is the straight uniform motion, and it minimises the action"
ex-cm07-free-particle-straight-lines.physical_scope: "A worked check of the stationary-action equivalence on the free one-label model: zero force map, zero potential, Cartesian Lagrangian of a free particle; on every closed time interval the stationary curves are exactly the affine uniform motions, for each pair of endpoint configurations there is exactly one, and the action difference to the stationary curve is a nonnegative quadratic functional of the variation, so the stationary curve is a minimiser within the fixed-endpoint class. All quantities are model values under the declared idealization of a particle subject to no force."

ex-cm07-nonholonomic-unrestricted-action.title: "The unrestricted action principle fails for the nonholonomic constraint z' = x y': the d'Alembert motion is not vakonomic"
ex-cm07-nonholonomic-unrestricted-action.physical_scope: "A worked check on the nonholonomic constraint z' = x y' with unit mass and zero applied force: the d'Alembert motion from the stated initial data has strictly positive y' and nonzero y'' on the positive half-line, so it cannot satisfy the vakonomic (unrestricted-action) equations of the same constraint, which force y'' to vanish wherever x'' does. Consequently the unrestricted action principle is not a substitute for the d'Alembert prescription on this branch. The example reports exact model computations, not measurements."

ex-cm07-oscillator-stationary-saddle-che.title: "The harmonic oscillator on a long interval: the stationary curve is neither a local minimum nor a local maximum"
ex-cm07-oscillator-stationary-saddle-che.physical_scope: "A worked check that stationarity is not minimisation, on the one-dimensional harmonic oscillator model with positive stiffness: on intervals longer than pi divided by the angular frequency, arbitrarily small fixed-endpoint variations around the zero stationary curve produce both strictly larger and strictly smaller actions, so the stationary curve is neither a local minimiser nor a local maximiser; on shorter intervals every sine-mode variation in the checked family increases the action. The computation uses exact model actions and exact trigonometric integrals; no experimental values are reported."

ex-cm07-pendulum-constraint-elimination-.title: "The planar pendulum by constraint elimination: kinetic metric, Lagrange equation and the ideal reaction recovered"
ex-cm07-pendulum-constraint-elimination-.physical_scope: "A worked check of the constraint-elimination theorem on the planar pendulum model: one particle of mass m constrained without friction to a circle of radius l in the plane z=0 under a uniform downward field; the parametrization by the angle gives kinetic metric m l^2, substituted potential -m g l cos(theta), the pendulum equation theta-ddot = -(g/l) sin(theta), and the reaction as a normal multiple with the explicit multiplier, so the parametrized solutions are exactly the ideal constrained motions. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization."

ex-cm07-polar-coordinate-kinetic-metric-.title: "Cylindrical coordinates for one label: the kinetic metric m diag(1, r^2, 1) and the coordinate form of the model's equation"
ex-cm07-polar-coordinate-kinetic-metric-.physical_scope: "A worked check of the coordinate-covariance theorem on cylindrical coordinates for one labelled particle of mass m in a declared potential presentation: the substituted Lagrangian has kinetic metric m diag(1, r^2, 1), the coordinate Euler-Lagrange equations are exactly the Cartesian equation written in the cylindrical frame, and the Cartesian stationary curves correspond to the coordinate solutions. All quantities are model values under the declared potential; no measurement is reported."

ex-cm07-total-derivative-gauge-check.title: "A total-derivative Lagrangian on explicit data: the endpoint term and the unchanged equations"
ex-cm07-total-derivative-gauge-check.physical_scope: "A worked gauge check on the free one-label model: adding the total time derivative of F(t,x)=alpha*t*x to the free Lagrangian changes the action by the endpoint value alpha(b x(b) - a x(a)) and leaves the Euler-Lagrange expression equal to the original one on every curve, hence leaves the stationary curves and the model's equation of motion unchanged; the potential normalization U + gamma t is the special case F = -gamma*t^2/2. The values are exact model values of a declared computation."

ex-cm08-pair-potential-charges-check.title: "A two-label pair-potential model: translation, rotation, boost and energy charges verified on the model class and on an explicit rigid-rotation motion"
ex-cm08-pair-potential-charges-check.physical_scope: "A worked check of the conservation statements of the pair on a two-label pair-potential model: for a potential depending on the labels through a C^2 function of the squared separation, the pair force is antisymmetric and central; the translation condition of the momentum theorem and the rotation condition of the angular-momentum theorem hold identically for every field direction and axis; the momentum, angular-momentum, boost and energy charges are therefore conserved along every motion of this model class; and an explicit rigid-rotation motion with a Hooke-type pair potential is verified together with its charges and a numerical instance. All values are model values of the declared idealization; the example reports no measurement and asserts no property of any physical interaction."

ex-cm08-rotating-chart-hamiltonian-not-m.title: "An oscillator observed in a uniformly rotating chart: the conserved chart Hamiltonian is not the inertial mechanical energy"
ex-cm08-rotating-chart-hamiltonian-not-m.physical_scope: "A worked computation of the moving-chart energy bookkeeping on an explicit model: the one-label isotropic oscillator with potential U = k |x|^2 / 2, observed in a chart rotating uniformly about the third axis; the substituted Lagrangian, its Legendre data and its Hamiltonian are computed, the difference identity between the chart Hamiltonian and the inertial mechanical energy is verified as the pairing of the chart's angular velocity with the momentum, an explicit circular motion with k = m omega^2 is shown to have chart Hamiltonian zero and inertial mechanical energy m omega^2 r^2, and a numerical instance is evaluated. All values are model values of the declared idealization; the example reports no measurement and asserts no property of an apparatus."

ex-cm08-time-dependent-potential-breaks-.title: "A one-label model with a time-dependent potential: the time-translation identity fails and the mechanical energy changes at the rate of the explicit time dependence"
ex-cm08-time-dependent-potential-breaks-.physical_scope: "A worked model check inside the framework: a one-label model in the three-dimensional force branch whose potential depends explicitly on time through a prescribed vector drive f(t), with force -k x + f(t); the time-translation identity of the pair holds exactly when the drive is constant, the mechanical energy changes at the rate -f'(t) . x along motions, and for the sinusoidally driven specialisation an explicit global motion is exhibited whose energy derivative at a stated time is nonzero, together with a numerical instance. All values are model values of the declared idealization; the drive is adopted external data, and the example reports no measurement."

ex-cm08-uniform-field-breaks-translation.title: "The uniform-force model: translation and boost charges fail across the field while the energy survives, with exact rates and a numerical instance"
ex-cm08-uniform-field-breaks-translation.physical_scope: "A worked model check inside the framework: the one-label uniform-force model with its potential presentation U = -m g . x, its explicit maximal motion, the failure of the translation and boost charges in directions with a nonzero component along the field, with the exact rates predicted by the sharpness clauses, a numerical instance at an explicit time, and the survival of the mechanical energy because the potential has no explicit time dependence. All values are model values in a declared idealization; the example reports no measurement and asserts no property of any field of nature."

ex-cm09-cubic-potential-error-check.title: "A cubic-potential chart system: the exact quadratic remainder, the explicit error constants and a checked finite-time bound"
ex-cm09-cubic-potential-error-check.physical_scope: "A worked instance of the finite-time linearization error bound: the one-dimensional chart system with constant mass m, potential U(q) = k q^2/2 + lambda q^3/6 and field G(q,v) = (v,-(kq+lambda q^2/2)/m), whose translated field has the exact quadratic remainder -(lambda/(2m)) delta q^2, giving the exact constants C = |lambda|/(2m) and L = max(1,(k+|lambda|r/2)/m) on the ball of radius r; a numerical instance with m=k=lambda=1, r=1, delta=10^-2 and T=1 checks the smallness condition delta exp(LT) = 0.04482 < 1 and the bound 2.73 x 10^-3, and the case lambda=0 reduces the field to its linearization with C=0. All quantities are exact-arithmetic evaluations of model formulas; no measurement or empirical claim is present."

ex-cm09-degenerate-oscillator-subspace.title: "A doubly degenerate quadratic model: every direction is a mode, the modal basis is not intrinsic, and coupling splits the double frequency"
ex-cm09-degenerate-oscillator-subspace.physical_scope: "A worked instance of degeneracy in the coupled quadratic model: two identical uncoupled oscillators, M = m I, K = k I, with the double modal stiffness k/m, the full two-dimensional eigenspace, the four-parameter family of motions, the non-intrinsic status of every modal basis and the splitting of the double frequency into k/m and (k+2c)/m when a coupling c>0 of the two-mass model is switched on. The parameters are model data; the example asserts no measured frequency and no general stability-of-degeneracy theorem."

ex-cm09-double-pendulum-linear-modes.title: "The equal-arm double pendulum in the linear approximation: the slow same-side mode, the fast opposite-side mode and the bounded modal motions"
ex-cm09-double-pendulum-linear-modes.physical_scope: "A worked instance of the coupled quadratic model: the two-angle small-oscillation data M = m l^2 [[2,1],[1,1]], K = m g l diag(2,1) attributed to the linearisation of an equal-mass equal-length planar double pendulum, with its two modal data (the slower same-side mode of frequency sqrt((g/l)(2-sqrt2)) and the faster opposite-side mode of frequency sqrt((g/l)(2+sqrt2))), the general bounded modal motion and the pure-mode data. The example verifies the quadratic model on the declared matrices; it does not derive the pendulum Lagrangians, does not control the error of the linear approximation at finite amplitude and asserts no measured period."

ex-cm09-forced-resonant-mode-check.title: "A drive along the in-phase pattern of the two-mass chain: resonance exactly at that mode's frequency and a bounded steady response off resonance"
ex-cm09-forced-resonant-mode-check.physical_scope: "A worked instance of the forced coupled quadratic model: the two equal-mass chain of the companion example with a prescribed sinusoidal generalized force J(t)=F cos(Omega t) u_+ along the in-phase pattern, the modal force components (F/m,0), the unbounded resonance at Omega = sqrt(k/m) with the explicit linearly growing modal motion, the bounded steady response of amplitude |F|/(2c) at Omega = sqrt((k+2c)/m), and the boundedness of every motion for Omega^2 not equal to k/m. The drive is prescribed external data; no back-reaction, measured response or empirical value is asserted."

ex-cm09-triatomic-translation-zero-mode.title: "A linear triatomic chain: the translation zero mode, the antisymmetric stretch and the symmetric stretch, with the corrected frequency comparison"
ex-cm09-triatomic-translation-zero-mode.physical_scope: "A worked instance of the coupled quadratic model: a linear chain of three labels with masses m, M, m joined by identical nearest-neighbour springs of stiffness k, modelled by the quadratic stiffness matrix k[[1,-1,0],[-1,2,-1],[0,-1,1]], with its three modal patterns (translation at zero modal stiffness, antisymmetric stretch at sqrt(k/m) and symmetric stretch at sqrt((k/m)(1+2m/M))), the general motion, the affine translation zero mode and the corrected frequency ordering omega_3>omega_2. The parameters are model data with declared units; the example asserts no measured molecular frequency and no empirical identification of the chain with a real molecule."

ex-cm09-two-mass-spring-modes.title: "Two coupled masses on a line: the in-phase and anti-phase normal modes, their frequencies, mode-energies and the zero-stiffness translation mode"
ex-cm09-two-mass-spring-modes.physical_scope: "A worked instance of the coupled quadratic model: two equal masses m on a line joined by a coupling spring c with outer springs k to fixed points, the explicit normal modes, frequencies sqrt(k/m) and sqrt((k+2c)/m), the single-mode initial data, the conserved mode energies, and the zero-stiffness case k=0 in which the pair's translation is an affine zero mode and only the relative motion oscillates. The masses and spring constants are model parameters with declared units; no measured value, no realized apparatus and no empirical claim is present."

ex-cm09-unstable-quadratic-mode.title: "The inverted pendulum about its upward equilibrium: the negative modal stiffness, the exponential quadratic mode and the nonlinear instability"
ex-cm09-unstable-quadratic-mode.physical_scope: "A worked instance of an unstable quadratic direction: the planar inverted pendulum of mass m and length l about its upward equilibrium, with chart data M = m l^2 and U(theta) = m g l cos(theta) measured from the upward vertical, negative Hessian -m g l, the exact exponential motions of the small-oscillation model and the exponential escaping family of the quadratic model, together with the nonlinear Lyapunov instability of the upward equilibrium obtained from the hyperbolic-saddle theorem. The example is a conditional statement about the declared mathematical model; g, m and l are model parameters and no measured period or escape time is asserted."

ex-cm09-weak-damping-averaging-check.title: "An explicit weakly damped oscillator: the averaging constants and the energy-decay bound on five thousand oscillation periods"
ex-cm09-weak-damping-averaging-check.physical_scope: "A worked numerical instance of the weak-damping averaging estimate: the model m x'' + epsilon gamma x' + k x = 0 with m = 1 kg, k = 1 kg/s^2, epsilon = 10^-4 and gamma = 1 kg/s, initial rotating-frame amplitude zeta_0 = 1, ball radii R = 1/2 and rho = 1/4 and horizon parameter A = 1/2, verifying the smallness and trapping hypotheses with the exact constants M = 3 sqrt2/2, L = sqrt2, K = 2 pi (3 sqrt2 + 6) exp(sqrt2/2) and concluding that the mechanical energy tracks the averaged exponential exp(-t/10^4) within 2.63 x 10^-2 on the interval [0,5000]. The numbers are exact-arithmetic evaluations of the model formulas, not measurements; no apparatus, no observed decay and no empirical statement is present."

ex-cm11-free-top-checks.title: "Two explicit free-rotation models checked: principal-axis spins, a non-uniform symmetric-top motion with its invariants, and the linearized frequencies of an asymmetric top"
ex-cm11-free-top-checks.physical_scope: "Worked checks inside the torque-free branch of the rigid-material model of [[post-cm10-rigid-material]] on two declared inertia matrices: a symmetric model with body inertia matrix diag(1,1,2) and an asymmetric model with diag(1,2,3). The checks verify principal-axis spins and their invariants, an explicit non-uniform symmetric-top motion with conserved angular momentum and energy, and the linearized frequencies at the principal-axis spins of the asymmetric model. No measured value, no concrete body and no experiment is asserted; the numerical data are declared model parameters."

ex-cm11-heavy-top-steady-precession.title: "A steady precession of the heavy symmetric top checked on explicit data: the pivot balance, the two conserved momenta and the reduced energy"
ex-cm11-heavy-top-steady-precession.physical_scope: "A worked steady precession of the heavy symmetric top branch of [[post-cm11-heavy-top]] on declared parameters $A_c=2$, $C_c=1$, $m=1$, $d=1$, $g=1$ (so the pivot transverse moment is $A=3$) and the explicit angles $\\varphi(t)=t$, $\\theta=\\pi/3$, $\\psi(t)=2t$: the pivot balance is verified identically in time, the two conserved momenta are $a=7/2$ and $b=5/2$, the reduced energy is $19/4$, and the heavy-top system holds, so the reduction conclusions apply. All numbers are declared model data in the framework's units; no measurement, no concrete top and no experiment is asserted."

ex-cm11-intermediate-axis-escape.title: "Explicit escape from the intermediate-axis spin of the model with inertia diag(1,2,3): the constants, the perturbed invariant level, and the escape-time bound"
ex-cm11-intermediate-axis-escape.physical_scope: "A worked instance of the intermediate-axis instability of [[pthm-cm11-nonlinear-spin-stability]] on the declared model with body inertia matrix diag(1,2,3) and spin datum $l_0=e_2$: the instability constants, a perturbed datum on the same invariant level with the checked proximity bound, and the resulting escape time and escape radius. The numerical data are declared model parameters; no measurement, no concrete body and no experiment is asserted."

ex-cm12-mechanical-legendre-positive-met.title: "Positive kinetic metric: the fibre map $p = \\mathsf Mv$, the Hamiltonian and Hamilton's equations on explicit one- and two-label data"
ex-cm12-mechanical-legendre-positive-met.physical_scope: "A worked check of the Legendre transform on the model class with positive definite kinetic operator: a one-label particle of mass m in a uniform downward potential field, with the explicit momentum p = mv, Hamiltonian H = |p|^2/(2m) + mg x_3, Hamilton equations, and the exact falling solution through a prescribed initial datum; and a two-label free model with unequal masses, where the mass operator is not a scalar and the inverse branch is computed entrywise. All quantities are model values of the declared idealizations; no measurement is reported."

ex-cm12-moving-coordinates.title: "Moving coordinates: the substituted Hamiltonian of a spring on a uniformly moving support, its conservation and the non-conservation of the mechanical energy"
ex-cm12-moving-coordinates.physical_scope: "A worked check of the Hamiltonian description in a time-dependent chart: a one-label model with a spring whose equilibrium point is attached to a support moving uniformly at a prescribed velocity, described in the co-moving coordinate; the substituted Lagrangian has a velocity-linear term, the substituted Hamiltonian is conserved, it differs from the model's mechanical energy by the product of the support velocity and the momentum, and the mechanical energy changes at the rate of the explicit time dependence of the potential. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement is reported."

ex-cm12-pendulum-legendre.title: "The planar pendulum in Hamiltonian form: kinetic metric $ml^{2}$, substituted Hamiltonian $p^{2}/(2ml^{2}) - mgl\\cos\\theta$ and the reduced equation"
ex-cm12-pendulum-legendre.physical_scope: "A worked check of the Hamiltonian reformulation on the planar pendulum of the framework: one label of mass m constrained without friction to a vertical circle of radius l under a uniform downward field, parametrized by the angle; the kinetic metric is ml^2, the substituted Hamiltonian is p^2/(2ml^2) - mgl cos(theta), Hamilton's equations reduce to theta-double-dot = -(g/l) sin(theta), and the system is equivalent to the ideal constrained motion with its reaction recovered by the elimination theorem. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement is reported."

ex-cm12-shifted-momentum.title: "Shifted momentum from a total-derivative modification: $p' = p + F_x$, $H' = H - F_t$ and unchanged motion on explicit data"
ex-cm12-shifted-momentum.physical_scope: "A worked check of the momentum shift produced by a total-derivative modification of a declared potential presentation: for a one-label model with mass m and a C^2 gauge function F(t,x) = alpha t x_1, the modified chart Lagrangian has fibre derivative p' = p + alpha t e_1, shifted Hamiltonian H' = H - alpha x_1 read at the shifted momentum, and Hamilton system equivalent to the original one; an explicit free-particle computation shows H' differs from the mechanical energy while the motion is unchanged. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement is reported."

ex-cm13-free-particle-flow-generating-fu.title: "The free particle of the model: the flow $Q=q+(t/m)p$ generated by the first-kind function $S_t(q,Q)=-m\\lvert Q-q\\rvert^{2}/(2t)$, the projection check and the exact change of $\\lambda$"
ex-cm13-free-particle-flow-generating-fu.physical_scope: "A worked generating-function computation for the declared one-label free-particle presentation: the explicit free Hamiltonian flow, its first-kind generating function $S_t$ with the mixed-Hessian determinant, the invertibility of the $(q,Q)$-projection for $t\\neq0$, the degeneration of the generating data at $t=0$, and the exact change of the canonical one-form along the flow. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement is reported."

ex-cm13-fundamental-brackets-and-evoluti.title: "Fundamental brackets and Bracket evolution on explicit one-label data: $\\{x^a,H\\}=p_a/m$, $\\{p_a,H\\}=-U_{x^a}$, and the oscillator check"
ex-cm13-fundamental-brackets-and-evoluti.physical_scope: "A worked computation of the bracket of a declared one-label potential presentation: the fundamental brackets of the canonical coordinates, the bracket of the coordinates with the branch Hamiltonian reproducing velocity and force, and the evolution identity and energy constancy on the isotropic oscillator instance. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement is reported."

ex-cm13-isotropic-oscillator-flow-symple.title: "The isotropic oscillator of the model: explicit solution, the determinant and matrix tests on each two-dimensional block, and the area and energy checks"
ex-cm13-isotropic-oscillator-flow-symple.physical_scope: "A worked verification of the symplectic and volume-preserving character of the model's Hamiltonian flow on the isotropic oscillator instance: the explicit solution of the one-label model with potential $(k/2)\\lvert x\\rvert^{2}$, the block matrix identity and unit determinant of its time-$t$ map, the area and six-volume checks on explicit boxes, and the constancy of the oscillator energy. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement is reported."

ex-cm13-point-transformation-generating-.title: "The point transformation of the model: the chart transition $(q,P)\\mapsto(X(q),DX(q)^{-\\mathsf T}P)$ is generated in the second kind, has a nowhere invertible $(q,Q)$-projection, and is contrasted with the momentum shift"
ex-cm13-point-transformation-generating-.physical_scope: "A worked projection and generating-function computation for the declared potential presentation: a genuine chart $X$ of the configuration domain induces the momentum chart transition $(q,P)\\mapsto(X(q),DX(q)^{-\\mathsf T}P)$, which is generated in the second kind by $S(q,P)=P\\cdot X(q)$, has unit determinant, and fails the first-kind projection hypothesis identically; the degenerate case is contrasted with the momentum shift, whose second-kind generating function is global. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization; no measurement is reported."

ex-cm13-verlet-map-of-the-mechanical-spl.title: "The velocity-Verlet step of the model's mechanical splitting is a canonical map of the presentation: exact flows of the drift and kick, unit determinant, and the oscillator check"
ex-cm13-verlet-map-of-the-mechanical-spl.physical_scope: "A worked verification that the velocity-Verlet step of the declared one-label potential presentation is a canonical map: the drift and kick are the exact time-$h$ flows of the kinetic and potential parts of the branch Hamiltonian, the composite satisfies the matrix identity in exact arithmetic, and the isotropic-oscillator instance is checked explicitly with unit determinant. All quantities are model values of the declared idealization in exact arithmetic; no measurement or roundoff claim is made."

ex-cm14-harmonic-oscillator-hamilton-jac.title: "The harmonic model worked through: an explicit complete integral, its characteristic motion, and the action-angle chart with $I=\\oint p\\,dx$ and period-one frequency $1/T$"
ex-cm14-harmonic-oscillator-hamilton-jac.physical_scope: "A worked instance of the Hamilton-Jacobi and action-angle items inside the declared harmonic model of the framework's force branch: for one label of mass $m>0$ and spring constant $k>0$, the explicit family $S$ is a complete integral of the model's Hamilton-Jacobi equation wherever $\\sin(\\omega t)\\neq0$; its characteristic curves are the harmonic motions with $\\beta=S_\\alpha$ constant; and the explicit chart $(\\theta,I)$ is canonical with $H=I/T$, $\\dot I=0$, $\\dot\\theta=1/T$ and $I=\\oint p\\,dx$, in the period-one convention, with the radian rescaling recovering the sources' chart. The example asserts no measured value, no claim that a real oscillator realizes the model, and no global extension of $S$ across the conjugate times $\\omega t\\in\\pi\\mathbb Z$."

ex-cm14-kepler-radial-action-check.title: "The gravitational two-body model on an elliptic orbit: two simple turning points of the effective potential and $J_{\\mathrm a}'(E)=T/(2\\pi)=\\sqrt{\\mu/\\kappa}\\,a^{3/2}$"
ex-cm14-kepler-radial-action-check.physical_scope: "A worked instance inside the two-label gravitational model of the framework's force branch: for an elliptic relative orbit ($j=Je_3$, $J>0$, $E<0$, eccentricity $0\\le e<1$), the Kepler effective potential has exactly two simple turning points on the energy window between its minimum and $0$; the one-dimensional action variable of the radial problem is $C^1$ there with derivative $T/(2\\pi)$; and the radial quadrature is the orbital period, so $J_{\\mathrm a}'(E)=T/(2\\pi)=\\sqrt{\\mu/\\kappa}\\,a^{3/2}$ with $T^2=4\\pi^2\\mu a^3/\\kappa$. The example uses only the model's declared couplings $\\kappa=G_{\\mathrm N}m_1^{g}m_2^{g}$ and masses; no measured value of $G_{\\mathrm N}$ and no empirical premise is used, and no real orbit is claimed to obey the model."

ex-cm14-oscillator-caustic-check.title: "The conjugate time of the harmonic model: the complete integral's mixed derivative is unbounded and the characteristic family refocuses at $\\omega t\\in\\pi\\mathbb Z$"
ex-cm14-oscillator-caustic-check.physical_scope: "A worked warning inside the declared harmonic model of the framework's force branch: the explicit complete integral of the oscillator's Hamilton-Jacobi equation is defined only on the time strips between the conjugate times $\\omega t\\in\\pi\\mathbb Z$; its mixed derivative $S_{x\\alpha}=-m\\omega\\csc(\\omega t)$ is unbounded as those times are approached; and the characteristic family through a fixed event refocuses there (all members with the same initial position pass through the same point a half-period later), so the map from the family's label to the position degenerates. The example asserts no measured value and no claim about any apparatus; it exhibits why the Hamilton-Jacobi statements of this page are local in time and carry no claim across a caustic."

ex-cm15-control-volume-check.title: "A declared smooth open flow: the uniform expansion $\\rho=\\rho_0e^{-3\\alpha t}$, $u=\\alpha x$ satisfies the control-volume identities on fixed and material regions, and an ideal elbow illustrates the inlet/outlet decomposition"
ex-cm15-control-volume-check.physical_scope: "Two declared checks of the smooth open-flow bookkeeping: (i) the exact uniform-expansion model $\\rho(t)=\\rho_0e^{-3\\alpha t}$, $u(t,x)=\\alpha x$, $p=p_0-\\rho\\alpha^2\\lvert x\\rvert^2/2$, whose fields satisfy the adopted local balances and whose fixed-ball and material-ball control regions satisfy the mass and momentum rates of the moving-control-region theorem; (ii) an idealised steady elbow with declared inlet/outlet data, where the inlet/outlet split gives the mass flux $0.4\\,\\mathrm{kg\\,s^{-1}}$ and the dynamic force $\\lvert\\dot m(v_{\\mathrm{out}}-v_{\\mathrm{in}})\\rvert\\approx3.578\\,\\mathrm{N}$ once the pressure part is declared negligible. Both are conditional computations on declared fields; the example reports no measurement and no solution of a boundary-value problem."

ex-cm15-hard-sphere-reflection-check.title: "Elastic reflection from a fixed sphere: the branch $b=a\\cos(\\theta/2)$, the uniform density $a^2/4$ and the total $\\pi a^2$ of a contact model"
ex-cm15-hard-sphere-reflection-check.physical_scope: "A declared contact model of a reduced label of mass $\\mu$ reflecting elastically from a fixed impenetrable sphere of radius $a$: the reflection rule reverses the normal velocity component and preserves the tangential component, so that speed and angular momentum are conserved across the contact; the example computes the branch $b=a\\cos(\\theta/2)$, the uniformly constant cross-section density $a^2/4$ and the truncated total $\\pi a^2$, and records that this is a contact (impulse) model outside the $C^2$ finite-range hypothesis of the central-scattering theorem, so its finite total does not contradict the Coulomb forward divergence. The data are declared model data; the example reports no observation and no measured value."

ex-cm15-impact-check.title: "A declared-data impact check: $m_1=2\\,\\mathrm{kg}$, $m_2=6\\,\\mathrm{kg}$, $v_1^-=3\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$, $v_2^-=-1\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$, with elastic, semi-elastic and sticking outcomes"
ex-cm15-impact-check.physical_scope: "A declared-data check of the adopted collinear impact model: masses $2$ and $6\\,\\mathrm{kg}$ with one-dimensional velocities $3$ and $-1\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$ along the contact direction, for coefficients of restitution $e=1,\\frac12,0$; the example verifies total momentum continuity, the impulse $J=-9\\,\\mathrm{N\\,s}$ at $e=\\frac12$, the post-impact velocities, and the kinetic-energy changes $0,-9,-12\\,\\mathrm{J}$, all in SI units. Every number is declared model data substituted into the model formulas; the example reports no measurement and no empirical comparison."

ex-cm15-rocket-check.title: "A declared rocket check: mass $3-t\\,\\mathrm{kg}$ and constant exhaust speed $2\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$ relative to the body give $v(t)=2\\ln(3/(3-t))\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$ and show that $(mv)'=F$ fails"
ex-cm15-rocket-check.physical_scope: "A declared-data check of the open-body material accounting: a body of initial mass $3\\,\\mathrm{kg}$ losing mass at $1\\,\\mathrm{kg\\,s^{-1}}$ with no external force and ejecta of constant speed $2\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$ relative to the body has velocity $v(t)=2\\ln(3/(3-t))\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$ from rest, satisfies the material balance identities, and violates the naive closed-system law $(mv)'=F$; the example verifies the identities, the thrust $2\\,\\mathrm{N}$ and the failure of the naive law on declared model data. It reports no measurement, no engine data and no empirical comparison."

ex-cm15-rutherford-cutoff-check.title: "A declared-data Rutherford check: $\\alpha=1$, $\\theta=\\pi/2$, $(\\mathrm d\\sigma/\\mathrm d\\Omega)=4\\times10^{-24}\\,\\mathrm{m^2}$, the band values $\\pi b(\\theta_1)^2$ and the growth of the truncated total as $\\theta_1\\downarrow0$"
ex-cm15-rutherford-cutoff-check.physical_scope: "A numerical check of the repulsive-Coulomb model prediction on declared model data in SI units: reduced mass $2\\times10^{-26}\\,\\mathrm{kg}$, energy $10^{-18}\\,\\mathrm{J}$, angular momentum $4\\times10^{-34}\\,\\mathrm{kg\\,m^2\\,s^{-1}}$ and coupling $\\kappa=4\\times10^{-30}\\,\\mathrm{J\\,m}$ give $v_\\infty=10^4\\,\\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$, $b=2\\times10^{-12}\\,\\mathrm{m}$, $\\alpha=1$, scattering angle $\\pi/2$ and density $4\\times10^{-24}\\,\\mathrm{m^2}$; the angular band values $\\pi(b(\\theta_1)^2-b(\\theta_2)^2)$ and the small-angle growth $\\approx(16\\pi\\times10^{-24}\\,\\mathrm{m^2})/\\theta_1^2$ are checked. All numbers are declared model data fed into the model formulas; the example asserts no measurement, no uncertainty budget and no comparison with any experiment."

ex-cm16-isotropic-oscillator-return-map-.title: "The planar isotropic oscillator: the stroboscopic map at half period is minus the identity, every state is periodic, the periodic points are dense, and the map is neither mixing nor sensitive"
ex-cm16-isotropic-oscillator-return-map-.physical_scope: "A declared-data check of the page's discrete-time vocabulary on the planar isotropic oscillator with unit mass and unit stiffness: the flow is an explicit rotation of each coordinate plane, the stroboscopic map at period pi is minus the identity, at period 2pi it is the identity, the Poincare first-return map to the section y=0, vy>0 is the identity, every state is periodic, periodic points are dense in the phase plane, and the map fails topological mixing and sensitivity, so it is not chaotic in the stated sense. The check is model-data substitution; it reports no measurement."

ex-cm16-linearization-and-growth-checks.title: "Two declared linear models worked through: the harmonic flow has zero finite-time growth in every direction, while the repulsive linear model has exact rates $\\pm1$ and the positive Lyapunov exponent $1$ at its equilibrium"
ex-cm16-linearization-and-growth-checks.physical_scope: "A declared-data check of the page's finite-time growth definition and of the variational-equation supplier on two dimensionless linear mechanical models: the harmonic model M=K=1 has the rotation flow, whose derivative is orthogonal, so every finite-time tangent growth rate vanishes identically and every Lyapunov exponent that exists is zero; the repulsive linear model U=-q^2/2 has the hyperbolic flow, with exact rates +1 and -1 along the eigenvectors of the linearisation and Lyapunov exponent 1 at the equilibrium along the unstable direction. The check is model-data substitution, not a measurement and not a statement about chaotic behaviour."

ex-cm16-pendulum-equilibrium-checks.title: "The ideal pendulum on declared data: strict minimum and Lyapunov stability at the downward equilibrium, negative Hessian and instability at the upward equilibrium, the exact linearisation frequencies, and failure of attraction"
ex-cm16-pendulum-equilibrium-checks.physical_scope: "A declared-data check of the page's energy-stability theorem on the ideal planar pendulum: with mass 1 kg, length 1 m and g=9.81 m s^-2 in the angle chart, the downward equilibrium is a strict minimum, hence Lyapunov stable but not attracting, with purely imaginary linearisation frequencies; the upward equilibrium has a strictly negative Hessian, hence is unstable, with the real linearisation rates. All data are declared model data; no measurement and no empirical comparison is made."

ex-cm16-pulse-horseshoe-data-check.title: "The pulsed horseshoe on declared data: $a=100$, the radicand box $[74,126]$, the contraction factor $1/\\sqrt{74}$, the fixed points $1\\pm\\sqrt{101}$, and the physical bounds of the coded states at $\\ell_0=1\\,\\mathrm m$, $m=1\\,\\mathrm{kg}$, $\\omega_0=2\\pi\\,\\mathrm{s^{-1}}$"
ex-cm16-pulse-horseshoe-data-check.physical_scope: "A declared-data check of the constants and bounds in the page's pulsed-horseshoe theorem: at amplitude a=100 the coding box is R=13, the radicands lie in [74,126], the contraction factor is 1/sqrt(74), the fixed points are 1 plus or minus sqrt(101), the limiting kick satisfies K composed with the rotation = F, and with length scale 1 m, mass 1 kg and frequency scale 2 pi per second the coded states are bounded by 13 m in position and 26 pi kg m per second in momentum, with period (pi/2+delta)/(2 pi) seconds. All quantities are declared model data; the pulse-width threshold is not numerically evaluated and no measurement is involved."

ex-cm16-recurrence-volume-check.title: "A trapped one-label model: the compact energy sublevel of the radial quartic potential is invariant with finite phase volume, so the recurrence theorem applies, while the free model's energy sublevels are unbounded and the hypothesis fails"
ex-cm16-recurrence-volume-check.physical_scope: "A declared-data check of the page's recurrence theorem on a trapped one-dimensional model: for the unit-mass quartic potential U(q)=q^4/4 the energy sublevel {E<=E1}, E1>0, is compact with finite area bounded by 4(4E1)^{1/4}sqrt(2E1), invariant under the flow by energy conservation and compact continuation, so the recurrence theorem gives almost-everywhere infinite returns; in contrast the free model U=0 has unbounded energy sublevels and a nonrecurrent nonzero-velocity motion, showing the finite-volume hypothesis is not automatic. The check uses no measurement."

ex-cm17-channel-flow-and-no-slip-check.title: "Poiseuille and Couette channel flows of the viscous branch: explicit profiles, flux and wall data"
ex-cm17-channel-flow-and-no-slip-check.physical_scope: "A worked steady plane channel problem of the adopted incompressible Newtonian branch: the Poiseuille profile with pressure gradient 6, height 2 and viscosity 3 is verified against the model's momentum equation with zero body force, its flux per unit width 4/3 and centre speed 1 are computed, the Couette profile is verified with its nonzero curl, and the no-slip wall conditions are recorded as adopted ideal boundary data. The example reports no measurement."

ex-cm17-elastic-plane-wave-and-energy-ch.title: "A longitudinal plane wave in the linear elastic branch: stress, equation of motion and strain energy computed"
ex-cm17-elastic-plane-wave-and-energy-ch.physical_scope: "A worked longitudinal plane wave of the adopted linear elastic branch: explicit strain, stress, verification of the displacement equation at the longitudinal speed root((lambda+2mu_s)/rho_0) and the positive strain-energy density of the wave. The computation is exact within the branch and asserts no measurement and no completeness of plane waves."

ex-cm17-periodic-shear-exact-solution-ch.title: "Periodic shear fields: an exact steady Euler solution, failure for the viscous branch, and the classification of steady periodic shears"
ex-cm17-periodic-shear-exact-solution-ch.physical_scope: "Worked checks on the periodic cell of the adopted fluid branch: the sinusoidal shear is verified to be an exact steady solution of the inviscid (Euler) branch with zero pressure and to fail the local existence theorem's projected equation for the viscous branch, and the steady periodic shear fields of the viscous branch with no body force are classified: only constants survive. The example uses the periodic-cell idealization and reports no measurement."

ex-cm18-frame-change-of-an-observation-m.title: "Frame change of a declared protocol: how the prediction map and an additive error transform between two inertial frames"
ex-cm18-frame-change-of-an-observation-m.physical_scope: "A worked conditional computation of the frame behaviour of one declared protocol: a protocol whose readout is the position of one label at one observation time is described in a second inertial frame, and the prediction map and the additive error are transformed by the displayed affine law. The item asserts no measured position, no measured error and no frame-independent reading; it records that the prediction map and the error model are frame-relative data of a protocol."

ex-cm18-pendulum-calibration-proposal.title: "A proposed small-angle pendulum calibration of a gravitational parameter: linearized propagation and a bounded nonlinearity remainder on declared data"
ex-cm18-pendulum-calibration-proposal.physical_scope: "A worked, explicitly hypothetical calibration proposal inside the pendulum branch: the declared protocol reads a length and a duration and uses the small-angle period relation 4 pi^2 l / T^2 as its prediction map for a gravitational parameter, with the period relation declared as the model adopted from the cited treatments and the finite-amplitude discrepancy left as an unquantified model error. The item computes the first and second derivatives of the model function, the exactly propagated covariance of the linearization, and the bounded nonlinearity remainder on a declared box; it asserts no measured length, period, parameter value or uncertainty."

ex-cm18-uniform-motion-sampling-check.title: "Repeated observation of a uniform motion: prediction map, adopted IID sampling hypotheses and the resulting sample-mean bound on declared data"
ex-cm18-uniform-motion-sampling-check.physical_scope: "A worked conditional computation on a declared one-label force model with zero force: the motion with constant coordinate velocity is checked to be a motion, the protocol reads one position coordinate at one time, and under the adopted IID and second-moment hypotheses of the sampling model the sample mean of repeated readings satisfies the displayed variance identity and probability bound. All numerical values are declared model data and hypothetical illustration; no physical motion, apparatus reading, measured velocity or uncertainty is asserted."

lem-cm-mass-metric-positivity.title: "The mass metric is symmetric, positive semidefinite, and positive definite exactly when the configuration differential is injective"

post-cm02-drag.title: "The linear drag model: a phenomenological velocity-proportional resistance with a declared coefficient"
post-cm02-drag.physical_scope: "Adoption of a constitutive force model for the interaction of a labeled particle with a medium: a linear drag force $-c\\dot x$ with a declared coefficient $c\\ge0$, optionally combined with a constant applied force. The model is phenomenological and restricted: it is adopted for a stated regime (slow motion in a viscous medium, the range in which the linear/Stokes form is used), its coefficient is a model parameter depending on body and medium, and the model neglects the random component of the environment's force. The item asserts no measured value, no derivation of the coefficient from the equation of motion, and no claim that the model applies to a given real motion."

post-cm02-force-superposition.title: "Adopted force model: force maps, the equation of motion, additive composition of force contributions and frame covariance"
post-cm02-force-superposition.physical_scope: "Adoption of the framework's force branch: force maps as continuous, state-locally-Lipschitz vector-valued maps on a time window, an open configuration domain and velocity space, the equation of motion $m_i\\ddot x_i=F_i(t,x,\\dot x)$ in every inertial frame, pointwise additivity of declared force contributions, and the transformation rule that a force law must satisfy under a change of inertial frame. The postulate excludes impacts, dry and static friction, stochastic and distributional forcing, and constraint reactions; it asserts no measured value, no conservation law and no claim that any physical interaction is exactly of this form."

post-cm02-interactions.title: "Restricted interaction models: pair decompositions, antisymmetry and centrality options, potential forces and the gravitational branch"
post-cm02-interactions.physical_scope: "Adoption of restricted interaction models inside the force branch of [[post-cm02-force-superposition]]: a decomposition of the total force into external single-label forces and pair forces, the optional pair assumptions of antisymmetry and centrality, the branch of force maps that come from a scalar potential with the Euclidean gradient, and the optional Newtonian gravitational pair-potential model with gravitational coupling parameters distinct from the inertial masses. The item asserts no law of nature, no measured value and no conservation law; the identification of gravitational and inertial mass is recorded as a further empirical assumption, not adopted."

post-cm04-harmonic-model.title: "The harmonic (linear restoring) model: a declared linear force law with parameter $k>0$"
post-cm04-harmonic-model.physical_scope: "Adoption of the harmonic oscillator as a restricted one-dimensional model: configuration domain the whole line, fixed mass m>0, force law F(x)=-k x with declared spring constant k>0 of dimension mass per time squared, and potential U(x)=k x^2/2. The model is a linear idealization of a restoring force, adopted for a stated regime (small displacements from a stable equilibrium, in which the quadratic term of the potential is the adequate approximation, as in the sources' linearization procedure); the spring constant is model data whose value, if taken from measurement, is an empirical premise with its own conditions and uncertainty. The item asserts no value of k, no claim that the model applies to a given spring or oscillation, and no measured result."
